A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReferDINO and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures and references. The complete supplied documents support comparison, including v2's supplementary Sections A–F; v1 ends with references.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReferDINO benchmark results, component ablations, pruning experiments and qualitative predictions in Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: V2 retains original ReferDINO experiments and reports additional baseline, efficiency and qualitative results, including supplementary Tables 6–7 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The GroundingDINO adaptation, temporal tracker and decoder, grounding-guided mask decoder, pruning score, losses and sequence-selection procedure remain substantively unchanged. Expanded explanations of bilinear sampling and gradient propagation do not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use RefCOCO/+/g pretraining and evaluate Ref-YouTube-VOS, Ref-DAVIS17, A2D-Sentences, JHMDB-Sentences and MeViS. Additional efficiency comparisons and visual examples do not establish new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 introduces G-DINO+SH and G-DINO+DH, both augmented with temporal self-attention, across Tables 1–2. Grounded-SAM2 disappears from the four-dataset Table 1 and Figure 5, while its MeViS comparison survives in supplementary Table 6 alongside newly included AL-Ref-SAM2. Table 7 adds an efficiency comparison involving SgMg, MUTR and G-DINO+DH.

E3.justification: The principal training/evaluation scheme is retained, but the reported MeViS selection threshold changes from 0.2 to 0.3. Table 5 replaces the 20% and 65% pruning settings with 15% and 30%, and adds FPS evaluation at 360P. These establish limited protocol revisions without proving which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The temporal and attention-removal ablations remain, and the existing momentum-coefficient case study moves to Appendix E. V2 removes v1's isolated dot-product/CondInst mask-decoder comparisons, revises the pruning sweep, and adds comparative memory/latency analysis in Appendix D and qualitative cases in Figure 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, variability estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes ReferDINO's Swin-T J&F from 66.4 to 67.5 on Ref-YouTube-VOS and from 66.8 to 66.7 on Ref-DAVIS17. Table 5 substantially replaces accuracy, FLOP and memory values and adds FPS; new baseline and efficiency results appear throughout Tables 1–2 and 6–7. These are reported result changes, not established same-setting gains. V2 Section 5.2 still quotes 66.4, conflicting with its Table 1.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.3 and Appendix A add a computational-complexity derivation absent from v1. Equations 7–11 derive a geometric-series cost bound for retaining 1/k queries per layer and argue independence from decoder depth under that model. The original method equations remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The central GroundingDINO-to-RVOS contribution, three components and five-benchmark superiority claim remain. V2 adds an explicit real-time capability claim, emphasizing 51 FPS and approximately tenfold acceleration in the abstract and introduction, beyond v1's general decoding-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the mechanisms offered for the method's effectiveness: segmentation gradients improve grounding, text attention mitigates sampling noise, shared feature maps avoid dynamic-head memory costs, and time-varying text features improve temporal reasoning over static embeddings. It also interprets the new adaptation baselines and efficiency comparisons. These explanations go beyond v1's briefer component descriptions and performance interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 16 sampling points and, in Appendix B, FPN construction, loss weights, augmentations, training epochs, batch sizes, frame sampling, optimizer settings and eight A800 GPUs. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility without establishing corresponding setting changes. However, v1's specific sam2_hiera_large baseline configuration is no longer stated; the project-page access information is retained.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against parallel box/mask heads, static-text temporal modules and foundation models used primarily for preprocessing. New references include YOLO-World, DetCLIP, OnlineRefer, temporal collection and distribution, and several downstream foundation-model applications. Some earlier references, including Segment Anything and the single-scale vision-transformer work, are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and substantial portions of the method explanation are rewritten. The mask-decoder and temporal-enhancer subsections and their ablations reverse order, qualitative discussion is condensed, and supplementary Sections A–F organize additional and relocated material. Affiliations and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 1 drops the zebra example, Figure 2 is redrawn, Figure 5 removes Grounded-SAM2 rows, and Figure 7 moves to the supplement. V2 adds Figure 8 and Tables 6–7, swaps the component-ablation tables, and adds an FPS column to Table 5.

improvement.justification: The trained GroundingDINO baselines substantially strengthen evidence that the proposed adaptations contribute beyond the foundation model itself. Appendix B resolves important reproducibility gaps, while the complexity and timing analyses better substantiate efficiency claims. These gains outweigh the removal of some isolated controls and Grounded-SAM2 comparisons, although the unresolved Table 1 versus Section 5.2 numerical inconsistency weakens reporting reliability.
